turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K). Design
variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])
  - Fe (fraction in [0, 0.502513])
  - Nb (fraction in [0, 0.98])
  - C (fraction in [0, 0.972])
  - Pr (fraction in [0, 0.265043])
  - As (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - B (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Pb (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - Ce (fraction in [0, 0.28])
  - Mo (fraction in [0, 1])
  - V (fraction in [0, 0.9918])
  - Zn (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Ni (fraction in [0, 0.6])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: O=0.348837, Cu=0.227273, Ba=0.166667, Sr=0.142857, Y=0.2,
Ca=0.136364, La=0.39, Bi=0.260989, Fe=0.251256, Nb=0.49, C=0.486,
Pr=0.132521, As=0.25, B=0.5, Pb=0.25, Ce=0.14, Mo=0.5, V=0.4959, Zn=0.5,
Ni=0.3".
turns.answer_text:
Looking at the training data, the highest Tc values are dominated by copper-oxide superconductors:

- H2S = 185 K (uses H, S — not in our design variables)
- **Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 = 132 K** (Hg not allowed)
- **Ba2Ca2Cu3O = 126 K** (only O, Cu, Ba, Ca — all allowed!)
- Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O = 120.2 K (Tl not allowed)
- Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O = 109 K (Sb not allowed)
- Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O = 105.7 K (all elements allowed)

The clear pattern: cuprates with the **Cu:O layered structure, alkaline-earth (Ba/Sr/Ca) charge reservoirs**, and ~3 Cu per formula unit give the highest Tc. Elements like Fe, Ni, Zn, Nb, B, C, Mo, V, As, Pr, Ce, La in high fractions correspond to much lower Tc families, so they should be set to 0.

The best fully-allowed composition is Ba2Ca2Cu3O (Tc = 126 K). Its fractions (sum = 8):
- O = 1/8 = 0.125
- Cu = 3/8 = 0.375
- Ba = 2/8 = 0.25
- Ca = 2/8 = 0.25

All within observed ranges. A nearby alternative, Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O (105.7 K), confirms the Cu–Ca/Sr/Ba–O family robustness, but Ba2Ca2Cu3O is the best data point, so I adopt it, adding a small O increase (oxygen stoichiometry slightly above 1 per formula in many optimal cuprates like Y1Ba2Cu3O7 suggests slight O enrichment helps, but the 126 K sample itself used O=0.125, so I keep it).

Final: O=0.125, Cu=0.375, Ba=0.25, Sr=0.0, Y=0.0, Ca=0.25, La=0.0, Bi=0.0, Fe=0.0, Nb=0.0, C=0.0, Pr=0.0, As=0.0, B=0.0, Pb=0.0, Ce=0.0, Mo=0.0, V=0.0, Zn=0.0, Ni=0.0
